Linux user-systemd sysmon persistence drop (~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py + sysmon.service) AIInstallation High
Hunts the Linux-side persistence artefacts dropped by malicious LiteLLM: a Python implant at `~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py` registered as a user-systemd unit `~/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service`. Name choice mimics legit Microsoft Sysmon-for-Linux but the path differs. Rationale: Datadog Security Labs and Sonatype both confirm `~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py` and the user-systemd `sysmon.service` unit as the Linux persistence pair. The legit Microsoft Sysmon-for-Linux binary lives under `/opt/sysmon` or `/usr/sbin/sysmon` (never `~/.config` and never `.py`), so the path itself is the discriminator. Cross-checked against: • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/ • https://www.sonatype.com/blog/compromised-litellm-pypi-package-delivers-multi-stage-credential-stealer
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1036.005 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer experimenting with a personal cron/systemd helper that happens to be named sysmon (rare; check ownership)
  • DFIR responder restoring a captured artefact to a forensic VM under ~/.config (whitelist by VM hostname)
  • Configuration-management tooling deploying an internal helper named sysmon to user space (audit whether internal Ansible/Salt roles do this)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/var/lib/dfir/","/opt/forensics/") or DeviceName has_any ("forensic","sandbox","dfir-vm"))
Response runbook
Triage: `systemctl --user status sysmon`, read the .py contents (the malicious version makes outbound POSTs to models.litellm.cloud / checkmarx.zone — UC4). Contain: `systemctl --user disable --now sysmon && rm -rf ~/.config/sysmon ~/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service && systemctl --user daemon-reload`; isolate the host. Hunt: walk back for the litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8 install in UC1 and forward for C2 beacons in UC4. Treat as full credential compromise (the implant harvests SSH, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.docker, ~/.netrc, env-vars).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/.config/sysmon/" and FileName =~ "sysmon.py"
    or FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user/" and FileName =~ "sysmon.service"
    or FolderPath endswith "/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py"
    or FolderPath endswith "/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImFileEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where TargetFilePath has "/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py" or TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service"
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
  (Syslog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where SyslogMessage has_any ("/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py","/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service","systemctl --user enable sysmon","systemctl --user start sysmon")
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, Facility)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP LiteLLM Linux User-Systemd sysmon Persistence Drop
id: 3c7d5e1f-8a02-4b9c-bf1a-5e3d7c9f2a18
description: Detects the creation of ~/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py or ~/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service — Linux-side persistence dropped by malicious litellm 1.82.7/1.82.8.
references:
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
  - https://www.sonatype.com/blog/compromised-litellm-pypi-package-delivers-multi-stage-credential-stealer
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1543.002
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py'
      - '/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Microsoft Sysmon-for-Linux installs into /opt or /usr/sbin, never under ~/.config — this path is malicious
level: high
(source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog) (@file.path:*/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py OR @file.path:*/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service OR @process.command_line:*"systemctl --user enable sysmon"* OR @process.command_line:*"systemctl --user start sysmon"*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("/\\.config/(sysmon/sysmon\\.py|systemd/user/sysmon\\.service)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service") by host, user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/sysmon/sysmon.py" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/sysmon.service") by host, user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Kubernetes privileged-pod DaemonSet fan-out from compromised LiteLLM workload AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation step where the TeamPCP LiteLLM payload creates privileged pods on every node in a cluster to establish persistence and lateral movement. Pivots on K8s audit logs for create-pod/daemonset events with privileged/hostNetwork/hostPID flags and ≥3 node fan-out from a single principal. Rationale: Datadog Security Labs and Trend Micro both describe the LiteLLM 1.82.8 payload's Kubernetes module creating privileged pods on every node for persistence. The cross-node fan-out (NodesTouched ≥ 3) from one user combined with privileged/hostNetwork/hostPID flags is the article-specific signal — distinguishes from legit DaemonSets (CSI drivers, log shippers) by combining principal-novelty triage downstream. Defender and Falcon left empty because K8s control-plane audit isn't shipped to MDE/FDR in standard configs. Cross-checked against: • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/c/inside-litellm-supply-chain-compromise.html • https://futuresearch.ai/blog/litellm-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1610 T1611 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication Change
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit DaemonSet rollout: CSI driver (`csi-node`), CNI agent (`cilium`, `calico-node`), log shipper (`fluent-bit`, `datadog-agent`), security agent (`falcon-sensor`)
  • Cluster admin manually creating a debug privileged pod on each node for troubleshooting
  • Helm upgrade of a privileged add-on (cert-manager webhook, ingress-nginx in privileged mode)
  • kured / node-maintenance operators that create per-node helper pods
Suppression filter
| where not (Username has_any ("system:serviceaccount:kube-system","system:serviceaccount:kube-public","system:serviceaccount:datadog","system:serviceaccount:falcon","system:serviceaccount:cilium","system:serviceaccount:calico-system") or Namespace in ("kube-system","kube-public","gke-system"))
Response runbook
Triage: pull the RequestObject and check the container image — if it's an unfamiliar registry / contains `litellm` / matches the TeamPCP IOC images, treat as confirmed. Check the principal — is it a service account that should be allowed to create privileged pods? Contain: revoke the principal's token (`kubectl delete secret <sa-token>` + rotate), apply a Kyverno/OPA-Gatekeeper policy blocking privileged: true outside system namespaces, and `kubectl delete daemonset/pods` matching the IOC labels. Hunt: walk back to the source pod — did one of its containers run `pip install litellm` (UC1)? Pull its egress logs for the C2 IOCs in UC4.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Verb in ("create","patch")
| extend Resource = tostring(ObjectRef.resource), Namespace = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace), Name = tostring(ObjectRef.name)
| where Resource in ("pods","daemonsets")
| extend RO = tostring(RequestObject)
| where RO has_any ('"privileged":true','"hostNetwork":true','"hostPID":true','"hostIPC":true')
| extend NodeName = extract(@'"nodeName"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', 1, RO)
| summarize NodesTouched = dcount(NodeName), Pods = make_set(Name, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), Sample = any(RO)
            by Username, Namespace, Resource
| where NodesTouched >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:kubernetes.audit @verb:(create OR patch) @objectRef.resource:(pods OR daemonsets) (@requestObject.spec.containers.securityContext.privileged:true OR @requestObject.spec.hostNetwork:true OR @requestObject.spec.hostPID:true OR @requestObject.spec.hostIPC:true)
CLOUD
index=k8s_audit sourcetype IN ("kube:apiserver:audit","aws:eks:audit","gcp:gke:audit") verb IN ("create","patch") objectRef.resource IN ("pods","daemonsets")
| spath input=requestObject path=spec.containers{}.securityContext.privileged output=privileged_arr
| spath input=requestObject path=spec.hostNetwork output=hostNet
| spath input=requestObject path=spec.hostPID output=hostPid
| spath input=requestObject path=spec.nodeName output=nodeName
| where 'privileged_arr'="true" OR hostNet="true" OR hostPid="true"
| stats dc(nodeName) as NodesTouched, values(objectRef.name) as Pods, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime by user.username, objectRef.namespace
| where NodesTouched >= 3
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] npm/node postinstall hook spawning interpreter and reaching new C2 host (Axios-style dropper) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Axios npm Package Compromised: Supply Chain Attack Delivers Cross-Platform RAT
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PowerShell masquerading as Windows Terminal at %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe (Axios RAT Windows stage) · [LLM] Linux Python RAT orphaned via nohup python3 /tmp/ld.py (Axios npm payload) · [LLM] macOS Axios RAT daemon spoof + ad-hoc codesign of hidden /private/tmp binary · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound C2 to sfrclak.com / 142.11.206.73:8000 (Axios npm RAT beacon) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Outbound C2 to sfrclak.com / 142.11.206.73:8000 (Axios npm RAT beacon) AICommand & Control High
Detects any host beaconing to the Axios npm supply-chain RAT C2 infrastructure at sfrclak[.]com or IP 142.11.206.73 on TCP/8000. The C2 endpoint is unique to the plain-crypto-js@4.2.1 dropper and is the highest-fidelity post-compromise indicator across Windows, Linux, and macOS payloads. Rationale: Anchored on the C2 IOCs explicitly named in the Snyk article (sfrclak[.]com:8000 and 142.11.206.73). Corroborated by Microsoft Security Blog, GTIG (UNC1069 attribution), Unit 42, Elastic Security Labs, Datadog Security Labs, and CISA advisory. The IP/domain pair has no legitimate use and is unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/04/01/mitigating-the-axios-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/north-korea-threat-actor-targets-axios-npm-package • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/axios-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/axios-one-rat-to-rule-them-all • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/axios-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/04/20/supply-chain-compromise-impacts-axios-node-package-manager
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071 T1195.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel sandbox or DFIR replay environment intentionally detonating the sample
  • Security researcher manually probing the IOC for IOC validation
  • Block-list firewall denial logs (DeviceAction=Deny) — still worth reviewing source host but not a compromise per se
  • Vulnerability scanner / asset-discovery tool reaching the IOC after IOC-feed ingest
  • Legacy network appliance with cached resolver pointing to old DNS record
Suppression filter
| where ActionType != "ConnectionFailed" and ActionType != "ConnectionDenied" | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe", "SenseIR.exe", "vulnerabilityScanner.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess on the source host (look for node.exe / node / npm / yarn / pnpm / bun as ancestor; pivot on InitiatingProcessParentFileName chain). Pull the host's package-lock.json / yarn.lock and grep for axios@1.14.1, axios@0.30.4, plain-crypto-js@4.2.1, @qqbrowser/openclaw-qbot, @shadanai/openclaw. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the device via Defender LiveResponse / EDR isolation. Block 142.11.206.73 and *.sfrclak.com at perimeter and DNS RPZ. Rotate any secrets exposed in CI/CD or developer env (NPM_TOKEN, AWS keys, GH_TOKEN, SSH keys, browser-saved creds). Step 3 — Hunt: search for follow-on indicators (%PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe, /tmp/ld.py, /Library/Caches/com.apple.act.mond), and broaden network search to any host that resolved sfrclak.com in the last 60 days even if no connection succeeded.
let C2Domains = dynamic(["sfrclak.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["142.11.206.73"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2IPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp asc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["sfrclak.com"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["142.11.206.73"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP in (C2IPs) or DestinationHostName has_any (C2Domains) or RequestURL has_any (C2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, SourceUserName, DeviceAction),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (C2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (C2IPs) or DstHostname has_any (C2Domains) or Url has_any (C2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, NetworkProtocol, Url)
| sort by TimeGenerated asc
title: Axios npm Supply-Chain RAT C2 Beacon (sfrclak.com / 142.11.206.73)
id: 0a8c9d2b-3e54-4f7a-9c41-2f6b7c8d9a01
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound network/DNS activity to the Axios npm supply-chain RAT C2 infrastructure (sfrclak.com and 142.11.206.73 on TCP/8000) deployed via the malicious plain-crypto-js@4.2.1 dependency.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/axios-npm-package-compromised-supply-chain-attack-delivers-cross-platform/
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/04/01/mitigating-the-axios-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/north-korea-threat-actor-targets-axios-npm-package
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/axios-supply-chain-attack/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp: '142.11.206.73'
  selection_domain:
    DestinationHostname|contains: 'sfrclak.com'
  selection_port:
    DestinationPort: 8000
  condition: selection_ip or selection_domain or (selection_ip and selection_port)
falsepositives:
  - None expected — IP/domain are attacker-controlled C2 with no legitimate business use
level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:3 AND (@DestinationIp:142.11.206.73 OR @DestinationHostname:*sfrclak.com* OR @DestinationHostname:*SFRCLAK.COM*)) OR (source:windows.security AND CIDR(@IpAddress, 142.11.206.73/32)) OR (source:linux.auditd AND (@network.destination.ip:142.11.206.73 OR @network.destination.name:*sfrclak.com*)) OR (source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) AND @DestinationPort:8000 AND CIDR(@DestinationIp, 142.11.206.73/32))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP6) RemoteAddressIP4="142.11.206.73" OR RemotePort=8000 AND RemoteAddressIP4="142.11.206.73"
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/sfrclak\.com$/i | groupBy([aid, DomainName], function=count())}, field=aid, include=[DomainName], mode=left)
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.src_ip) as src_ip values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.app) as app from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="sfrclak.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="142.11.206.73") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [ | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="sfrclak.com" OR DNS.query="*.sfrclak.com" by DNS.query host | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.src_ip) as src_ip values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.app) as app from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="sfrclak.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_ip="142.11.206.73") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="sfrclak.com" OR DNS.query="*.sfrclak.com" by DNS.query host | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
PowerShell masquerading as Windows Terminal at %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe (Axios RAT Windows stage) AIInstallation High
Detects the Windows second-stage Axios RAT payload: a VBScript drops a copy of powershell.exe to C:\ProgramData\wt.exe (impersonating Windows Terminal) and launches it with execution-policy bypass and hidden-window flags. Legitimate Windows Terminal lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps or Program Files — never %PROGRAMDATA%. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim Windows-stage IOC from Table 2 of the article: %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe with PowerShell masquerading as Windows Terminal and execution-policy bypass. The %PROGRAMDATA% path is the discriminator — legitimate Windows Terminal ships via the Microsoft Store and resides under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps. Corroborated by Microsoft Security Blog and StepSecurity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/04/01/mitigating-the-axios-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan • https://www.huntress.com/blog/supply-chain-compromise-axios-npm-package
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1059.001 T1059.005 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom enterprise app intentionally named wt.exe deployed to ProgramData by an SCCM package (rare — review packaging metadata)
  • Red-team / pentest engagement deploying a PowerShell beacon at this exact path
  • IT script-runner tool installed by an admin to ProgramData (verify with software inventory)
  • Malware-removal tool quarantine staging the file before deletion (look at parent — should be AV)
  • Developer self-built debugging stub mimicking the name (verify signing chain)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe", "MsSense.exe", "SenseIR.exe") | where FolderPath !contains @"\WindowsApps\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: hash the wt.exe under %PROGRAMDATA% (SHA256 should match one of 617b67a8…, 92ff0877…, fcb81618…); pull the InitiatingProcessFileName — expect node.exe / wscript.exe / cscript.exe as ancestor, often kicked off by npm.exe / yarn.exe / pnpm.exe. Step 2 — Contain: isolate host, kill wt.exe process, quarantine the binary, block its hash org-wide, and check for the parallel scheduled task / Run key persistence. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents from this host to 142.11.206.73 or sfrclak.com, and grep the host's package-lock.json for axios@1.14.1, axios@0.30.4, or plain-crypto-js@4.2.1; rotate any secrets reachable from the developer/CI environment.
let SuspectPaths = dynamic([@"c:\programdata\wt.exe", @"%programdata%\wt.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\ProgramData\" and FileName =~ "wt.exe")
     or (FileName =~ "wt.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-ExecutionPolicy Bypass", "-ep bypass", "-WindowStyle Hidden", "-w hidden", "-nop", "-noprofile"))
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\" and FolderPath !contains @"\Microsoft\WindowsApps\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath has @"\ProgramData\" and FileName =~ "wt.exe"
    | project DeviceName, DropTime=Timestamp, DroppedBy=InitiatingProcessFileName, DroppedByCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, DroppedSHA256=SHA256
  ) on DeviceName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectName = "wt.exe";
let BypassTokens = dynamic(["-ExecutionPolicy Bypass", "-ep bypass", "-WindowStyle Hidden", "-w hidden", "-nop", "-noprofile"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith @"\wt.exe"
    | where NewProcessName has @"\ProgramData\" or CommandLine has_any (BypassTokens)
    | where NewProcessName !contains @"\WindowsApps\"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetProcessName endswith @"\wt.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith @"\wt.exe"
    | where (TargetProcessName has @"\ProgramData\" or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (BypassTokens))
    | where TargetProcessName !contains @"\WindowsApps\"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName)
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
title: PowerShell masquerading as Windows Terminal at %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe (Axios npm RAT)
id: 1b9d0e3c-4f65-4087-aaef-3a7c8d9e0b12
status: experimental
description: Detects the Windows-stage Axios npm RAT payload — a PowerShell binary copied to C:\ProgramData\wt.exe (impersonating Windows Terminal) and launched with execution-policy bypass and hidden-window flags. Legitimate Windows Terminal never lives under %PROGRAMDATA%.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/axios-npm-package-compromised-supply-chain-attack-delivers-cross-platform/
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/04/01/mitigating-the-axios-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_path:
    Image|contains: '\ProgramData\'
    Image|endswith: '\wt.exe'
  selection_name_bypass:
    Image|endswith: '\wt.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
      - '-ep bypass'
      - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
      - '-w hidden'
      - '-nop'
      - '-noprofile'

      - '\Microsoft\WindowsApps\'
  condition: (selection_path or selection_name_bypass) and not filter_legit

  - None — legitimate Windows Terminal does not install to %PROGRAMDATA%
level: critical
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) AND (@EventID:(1 OR 4688)) AND (@Image:(*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe OR *\\programdata\\wt.exe OR *\\PROGRAMDATA\\wt.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.EXE) OR @NewProcessName:(*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe OR *\\programdata\\wt.exe)) AND -@Image:(*\\WindowsApps\\* OR *\\Program?Files\\WindowsApps\\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\programdata\\wt\.exe$/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\windowsapps\\/i

Linux Python RAT orphaned via nohup python3 /tmp/ld.py (Axios npm payload) AIInstallation High
Detects the Linux second-stage Axios RAT payload: a Python script written to /tmp/ld.py and detached from its parent shell via `nohup python3`. The exact file path and orphan-via-nohup pattern are distinctive to the plain-crypto-js dropper. Rationale: Hard-anchored on the verbatim Linux IOC from the article: '/tmp/ld.py' Python script launched via 'nohup python3' to detach as an orphan background process. The path and the nohup-orphan pattern are unique enough that single-event match is high-fidelity. Corroborated by Huntress, Elastic Security Labs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.huntress.com/blog/supply-chain-compromise-axios-npm-package • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/axios-one-rat-to-rule-them-all • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1564.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DevOps engineer ad-hoc placing a one-off Python script at /tmp/ld.py (rare and easily disambiguated by hash + git provenance)
  • Penetration test deliberately reproducing the IOC for detection validation
  • CI runner that uses /tmp as a scratch directory and happens to name a file ld.py (verify owner UID and ProcessTree origin)
  • DFIR responder running a reproduction sample in a contained lab
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("root", "systemd") or ProcessCommandLine has "nohup"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm /tmp/ld.py exists and pull its SHA256 (compare to 617b67a8…, 92ff0877…, fcb81618…); look for the parent process tree — expect node → sh/bash → nohup python3, often launched from a CI/CD runner during npm/bun install. Step 2 — Contain: kill the orphaned python3 process (`pkill -f /tmp/ld.py`), quarantine the file, block 142.11.206.73 / sfrclak.com at perimeter, and rotate any secrets in the host's env (especially CI_JOB_TOKEN, AWS_*, NPM_TOKEN, SSH agent). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to outbound connections from the host to 142.11.206.73 on TCP/8000, search package-lock.json across all repos that build on this host for axios@1.14.1, axios@0.30.4, plain-crypto-js@4.2.1, @qqbrowser/openclaw-qbot, @shadanai/openclaw.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where DeviceName !endswith ".local" or 1==1  // applies to all OS; Linux sensor populates this table when MDE for Linux is deployed
| where (FileName in~ ("python3", "python", "python3.10", "python3.11", "python3.12") and ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/ld.py")
     or (FileName =~ "nohup" and ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/ld.py")
     or (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "nohup" and FileName matches regex @"^python[0-9.]*$" and ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/ld.py")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath == "/tmp/" and FileName =~ "ld.py"
    | project DeviceName, DropTime=Timestamp, DroppedBy=InitiatingProcessFileName, DroppedByCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, DroppedSHA256=SHA256
  ) on DeviceName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DvcOs has_any ("Linux", "linux") or ActingProcessName matches regex @"/python[0-9.]*$" or ActingProcessName endswith "/nohup"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/ld.py" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/ld.py"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine),
  (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Facility in ("authpriv", "auth", "daemon", "user")
    | where SyslogMessage has "/tmp/ld.py" and (SyslogMessage has "nohup" or SyslogMessage has "python")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, SeverityLevel, SyslogMessage)
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

macOS Axios RAT daemon spoof + ad-hoc codesign of hidden /private/tmp binary AIInstallation High
Detects the macOS Axios RAT payload: the dropper writes a binary to /Library/Caches/com.apple.act.mond (impersonating an Apple background daemon) and, for follow-on `peinject` payloads, performs ad-hoc code signing on hidden binaries under /private/tmp (e.g. /private/tmp/.XXXXXX) with `codesign --force --deep --sign -` to bypass Gatekeeper. Rationale: Anchored on three verbatim macOS IOCs from the article body and Table 2: (1) the /Library/Caches/com.apple.act.mond drop path that spoofs an Apple daemon, (2) the `codesign --force --deep --sign -` ad-hoc signing primitive used to bypass Gatekeeper, and (3) the /private/tmp/.XXXXXX hidden-file staging pattern. Corroborated by Elastic Security Labs and GTIG (UNC1069). Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/axios-one-rat-to-rule-them-all • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/north-korea-threat-actor-targets-axios-npm-package • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/c/axios-npm-package-compromised.html
ATT&CKT1036.004 T1553.002 T1564.001 T1059.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Apple internal/beta software writing a similarly named cache file (verify code signature on the binary)
  • Developer building a CLI tool locally and ad-hoc signing a binary they placed in /private/tmp/. — verifiable via shell history and team context
  • Reverse engineer running the sample in an isolated VM for analysis
  • Red-team engagement reproducing the macOS payload to validate detection
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("Xcode", "xcodebuild", "swift")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: compute SHA256 of /Library/Caches/com.apple.act.mond and compare to 617b67a8…, 92ff0877…, fcb81618…; pull parent process — expect osascript → curl/python with sfrclak.com in command line. Step 2 — Contain: kill the RAT process (`launchctl kickstart` not applicable — direct `kill -9`), quarantine the daemon binary, remove any LaunchAgents/LaunchDaemons created by the RAT, block 142.11.206.73 / sfrclak.com at perimeter. Rotate keychain creds, AWS/GCP/AZ CLI tokens, npm tokens, SSH keys for the user. Step 3 — Hunt: search ImFileEvent for files written under /private/tmp/.* with subsequent codesign --sign - executions; pivot to outbound connections to 142.11.206.73 on TCP/8000; grep package-lock.json / yarn.lock / bun.lockb across the user's projects for axios@1.14.1, axios@0.30.4, plain-crypto-js@4.2.1.
let RatPath = "/Library/Caches/com.apple.act.mond";
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath has "/Library/Caches/" and FileName =~ "com.apple.act.mond"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "codesign"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "--force" and ProcessCommandLine has "--deep" and ProcessCommandLine has "--sign -"
    | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/private/tmp/\.[A-Za-z0-9]{4,}"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName),
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "osascript" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node", "npm", "yarn", "pnpm", "bun", "sh", "bash", "zsh")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "curl" or ProcessCommandLine has "/Library/Caches/" or ProcessCommandLine has "sfrclak"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFilePath has "/Library/Caches/com.apple.act.mond"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, DvcAction),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/codesign"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--force" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "--deep" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "--sign -"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/private/tmp/\.[A-Za-z0-9]{4,}"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName)
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

npm/node postinstall hook spawning interpreter and reaching new C2 host (Axios-style dropper) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the supply-chain-dropper pattern made famous by Axios/plain-crypto-js: node.exe (or node on Linux/macOS) invoked as a postinstall hook spawns a script interpreter (wscript / cscript / osascript / python / sh) that within 60s establishes an outbound TCP connection to a never-before-seen public host. Catches the technique even if the IOCs rotate. Rationale: Generalises the dropper signature described in the article — npm postinstall hook (`"postinstall": "node setup.js"`) → node.exe → script interpreter / curl / nohup → outbound to attacker C2. The `node parent + scripting child + outbound to never-seen public host within 60s` chain is the structural fingerprint of the plain-crypto-js technique and similar npm dropper supply-chain attacks. Corroborated against GTIG / UNC1069 write-up describing the same pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/north-korea-threat-actor-targets-axios-npm-package • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/axios-one-rat-to-rule-them-all • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/axios-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ • https://www.sans.org/blog/axios-npm-supply-chain-compromise-malicious-packages-remote-access-trojan
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate package postinstall hooks (node-gyp, sharp, esbuild, puppeteer) downloading native binaries from CDN — exclude known registry/CDN hosts in `KnownRegistries`
  • Husky / Lefthook git-hook installers spawning shell to wire up hooks
  • Local dev `npm install` of telemetry SDK that phones home on first launch
  • Build container running `npm ci` and pulling binaries from a known internal Artifactory / Verdaccio mirror
  • Bun lockfile-resolve step spawning curl to fetch a missing tarball
Suppression filter
| where not(ChildCmd has_any ("node-gyp", "prebuild-install", "@sentry/cli", "esbuild", "husky", "lefthook", "sharp/install.js", "puppeteer/install.js")) | where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("registry.npmjs.org", "github.com", "objects.githubusercontent.com", "cdn.jsdelivr.net", "unpkg.com", "nodejs.org", "pnpm.io", "bun.sh"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: list the packages installed in the immediate npm/yarn/bun session (correlate ProcTime to recent package-lock.json / yarn.lock mtime, or fetch `npm ls --depth=0` output via LiveResponse). Flag any package whose postinstall hook spawned a non-node interpreter or made a network call to a non-CDN host. Step 2 — Contain: if a confirmed malicious package is identified, isolate the host, kill the spawned interpreter chain, block the destination IP/host at perimeter, and pin known-good versions in the affected repos. Step 3 — Hunt: query all developer/CI hosts for installs of the suspect package in the last 30 days, broaden to other postinstall droppers (@qqbrowser/openclaw-qbot, @shadanai/openclaw), and rotate secrets in any CI/CD environment that ran the affected install.

let WindowSec = 60;
let PostInstallChildren = dynamic(["wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","python.exe","python3","python","sh","bash","osascript","nohup","curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget"]);
let KnownRegistries = dynamic(["registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","registry.npm.taobao.org","npmjs.com","npmjs.org","yarnpkg.com","pnpm.io","bun.sh","jsdelivr.net","unpkg.com","github.com","githubusercontent.com"]);
let NodeChildren = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.exe", "npm", "yarn.exe", "yarn", "pnpm.exe", "pnpm", "bun.exe", "bun")
         or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.exe", "npm", "yarn.exe", "yarn", "pnpm.exe", "pnpm", "bun.exe", "bun")
    | where FileName in~ (PostInstallChildren)
    | project ProcTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, ChildName=FileName, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, ParentName=InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessId;
let Beacons = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | where isnotempty(RemoteIP)

| join kind=inner Beacons on DeviceId
| where NetTime between (ProcTime .. ProcTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| where ChildName =~ NetProc or ProcessId == NetPID
| project ProcTime, NetTime, DelaySec=datetime_diff('second', NetTime, ProcTime), DeviceName, AccountName, ParentName, ParentCmd, ChildName, ChildCmd, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by ProcTime desc

let KnownRegistries = dynamic(["registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","npmjs.com","npmjs.org","yarnpkg.com","pnpm.io","bun.sh","jsdelivr.net","unpkg.com","github.com","githubusercontent.com"]);
let NodeChildren = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where ParentProcessName endswith "/node" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\npm.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/npm" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\yarn.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/yarn" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\pnpm.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/pnpm" or ParentProcessName endswith "/bun"
    | extend ChildLeaf = tolower(tostring(split(ActingProcessName, iff(ActingProcessName has "/", "/", "\\"))[-1]))
    | where ChildLeaf in (PostInstallChildren)
    | project ProcTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ChildLeaf, ChildCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId;
let Beacons = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where isnotempty(DstIpAddr)
    | where not(DstHostname has_any (KnownRegistries))
    | where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172.16." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172.17." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172.18." and DstIpAddr !startswith "127."
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, NetworkProtocol;
NodeChildren
| join kind=inner Beacons on DvcHostname

| project ProcTime, NetTime, DelaySec=datetime_diff('second', NetTime, ProcTime), DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ChildLeaf, ChildCmd, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname

source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) AND (@ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR */node OR *\\npm.exe OR */npm OR *\\yarn.exe OR */yarn OR *\\pnpm.exe OR */pnpm OR */bun OR *\\bun.exe) OR @ParentCommandLine:*"npm install"* OR @ParentCommandLine:*"yarn install"* OR @ParentCommandLine:*"pnpm install"* OR @ParentCommandLine:*"bun install"* OR @ParentCommandLine:*postinstall*) AND (@Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\python.exe OR */python3 OR */python OR */bash OR */sh OR */osascript OR */nohup OR */curl OR */wget OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/python* OR /usr/local/bin/python* OR /bin/sh OR /bin/bash OR /usr/bin/nohup OR /usr/bin/osascript))

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

DeviceNetworkEvents

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a

references:

author: Clankerusecase

tags:

detection:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or SHA1 in~ ("617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766") or MD5 in~ ("617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("617b67a8e1210e4fc87c92d1d1da45a2f311c08d26e89b12307cf583c900d101", "92ff08773995ebc8d55ec4b8e1a225d0d1e51efa4ef88b8849d0071230c9645a", "fcb81618bb15edfdedfb638b4c08a2af9cac9ecfa551af135a8402bf980375cf", "2553649f2322049666871cea80a5d0d6adc700ca", "d6f3f62fd3b9f5432f5782b62d8cfd5247d5ee71", "07d889e2dadce6f3910dcbc253317d28ca61c766")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]

axios npm RAT C2 beacon to sfrclak.com / 142.11.206.73:8000 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects network egress to the campaign-exclusive C2 infrastructure used by the plain-crypto-js dropper after the compromised axios@1.14.1 / axios@0.30.4 packages execute their postinstall hook. The dropper retrieves platform-specific payloads from http://sfrclak[.]com:8000/6202033 — any host contacting that IP or domain on any port is a near-zero-FP signal. Rationale: sfrclak.com and 142.11.206.73 (port 8000, URI /6202033) are unique campaign infrastructure for the plain-crypto-js RAT dropper — they have no legitimate use. Article corroborated by StepSecurity and Socket which independently published the same C2 IOC. axios RAT artifact dropped: com.apple.act.mond / wt.exe / ld.py with known SHA256 AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the three platform-specific RAT binaries dropped by plain-crypto-js@4.2.1's postinstall hook: /Library/Caches/com.apple.act.mond on macOS (masqueraded as Apple ACT daemon), %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe on Windows (PowerShell copy disguised as Windows Terminal), and /tmp/ld.py on Linux. Matches on both fixed hash and path patterns so it catches renamed-but-identical samples. Rationale: Drop paths are baked into the dropper code per platform (article + StepSecurity confirm identical paths), and the SHA256s give a hash-pinned signal even if attackers rename. Sigma uses 1-of-* across selections for cross-platform single-event coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan • https://socket.dev/blog/axios-npm-package-compromised

PowerShell copy masqueraded as Windows Terminal in %PROGRAMDATA% running 6202033.ps1 AIInstallation High
Hunts the Windows-specific stage-2 chain of the axios RAT: plain-crypto-js's setup.js copies powershell.exe to %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe (mimicking Windows Terminal, which legitimately lives under \Program Files\WindowsApps), writes %TEMP%\6202033.vbs as a hidden launcher, and uses it to invoke %TEMP%\6202033.ps1 — a renamed-interpreter LOLbin pattern that bypasses powershell.exe-named telemetry. Rationale: Microsoft's real Windows Terminal (wt.exe) ships only under \Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_* — a wt.exe under \ProgramData\ is the exact masquerade described in the article. Pairing that with the literal 6202033 token (used as the URI path on the C2 and as the .vbs/.ps1 filename basename) and node.exe parents with plain-crypto-js/sfrclak strings keeps this scoped to the actual dropper chain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan • https://socket.dev/blog/axios-npm-package-compromised

    or (ParentProcessName endswith @"\node.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("6202033","plain-crypto-js","sfrclak"))
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType),
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where (TargetProcessName endswith @"\ProgramData\wt.exe")
    or (ParentProcessName endswith @"\ProgramData\wt.exe")
    or (TargetProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "6202033")
    or (TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "6202033.ps1")
    or (ParentProcessName has "node.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("6202033","plain-crypto-js","sfrclak"))
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: axios RAT Stage-2 — PowerShell Masqueraded as wt.exe in %PROGRAMDATA%
id: d3fab6e4-9a5f-4c02-b3d7-fab9e1c8d5f6
status: experimental
description: Detects the Windows stage-2 of the axios npm supply-chain RAT — PowerShell.exe copied to %PROGRAMDATA%\wt.exe (masquerading as Windows Terminal) and/or wscript/cscript launching the 6202033.vbs / 6202033.ps1 payload pair.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/axios-npm-compromised-maintainer-hijacked-rat
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/axios-compromised-on-npm-malicious-versions-drop-remote-access-trojan
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/13
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.005
  - attack.t1218
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_wt_image:
    Image|endswith: '\ProgramData\wt.exe'
  selection_wt_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\ProgramData\wt.exe'
  selection_vbs_token:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '6202033'
  selection_ps1_token:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '6202033.ps1'
  selection_node_dropper:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\node.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '6202033'
      - 'plain-crypto-js'
      - 'sfrclak'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - The legitimate Microsoft Windows Terminal binary is named wt.exe but resides under \Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_*\ — not under \ProgramData\. Any wt.exe in \ProgramData\ is suspicious.
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) AND ((@Image:(*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.EXE) OR @ParentImage:(*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.EXE) OR @NewProcessName:(*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe OR *\\ProgramData\\WT.exe)) OR (@Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\CSCRIPT.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*6202033*) OR (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\pwsh.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*6202033.ps1*) OR (@ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*6202033* OR *plain-crypto-js* OR *sfrclak*)))
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND (Processes.process="*6202033.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*\\Temp\\6202033*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wt.exe") AND Processes.process="*6202033.ps1*") OR (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd") AND Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*6202033*" OR Processes.process="*plain-crypto-js*" OR Processes.process="*sfrclak*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_path Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\ProgramData\\wt.exe") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND (Processes.process="*6202033.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*\\Temp\\6202033*")) OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wt.exe") AND Processes.process="*6202033.ps1*") OR (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd") AND Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*6202033*" OR Processes.process="*plain-crypto-js*" OR Processes.process="*sfrclak*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_path Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
